description: Standardized human-reviewed evaluation dataset for evidence grounding, cross-document contradiction detection, and claim provenance.

metadata.annotation_method: Dual-annotator consensus review of empirical findings and explicit contradictions

test_cases.question: How does GraphRAG improve over standard baseline RAG on global sensemaking questions?
expected_document_titles: GraphRAG: Unlocking LLM Discovery on Complex Information Networks
labeled_claims: GraphRAG combines knowledge graph construction with hierarchical summarization to answer global questions across entire corpora.
GraphRAG demonstrates substantial improvements in comprehensiveness and diversity compared to naive baseline RAG on complex sensemaking tasks.
Standard vector RAG struggles with global questions that require synthesizing connections across multiple disparate documents.
labeled_contradiction_pairs: naive vector retrieval is sufficient for global corpus understanding
standard vector RAG fails on global questions requiring cross-document synthesis

test_cases.question: What mechanisms are most effective for mitigating hallucinations in retrieval-augmented LLM architectures?
expected_document_titles: Hallucination Mitigation in Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
labeled_claims: External retrieval-augmentation significantly reduces factual hallucination rates compared to purely parametric LLM generation.
Citation validation mechanisms identify source mismatches and enforce strict evidence attribution.
Post-generation verification filters ungrounded model statements before presenting answers to researchers.

test_cases.question: What are the computational costs and latency trade-offs of knowledge graph traversal compared to vector search?
expected_document_titles: GraphRAG: Unlocking LLM Discovery on Complex Information Networks
Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
labeled_claims: Graph index construction incurs higher upfront token costs and processing time due to LLM-driven entity extraction.
Vector search provides millisecond-level approximate nearest neighbor lookup with minimal graph overhead.
Graph traversal requires multi-hop path exploration that can increase query latency if not pruned.
labeled_contradiction_pairs: knowledge graph indexing requires minimal computational investment
graph index construction incurs significant upfront token consumption

test_cases.question: Does dense vector retrieval universally outperform sparse lexical search across all research domains?
expected_document_titles: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
labeled_claims: Dense retrieval achieves superior semantic generalization on in-domain academic queries.
Sparse lexical retrieval (BM25) remains highly competitive or superior when searching exact technical identifiers, jargon, or out-of-distribution codes.
Hybrid retrieval combining dense semantic embeddings with BM25 lexical ranking achieves the most robust overall recall.
labeled_contradiction_pairs: dense retrieval universally supersedes sparse keyword search
BM25 outperforms dense vectors on rare technical identifiers and out-of-domain queries

test_cases.question: What are the quantum cryptographic key distribution benchmarks for superconducting qubits in the corpus?
How does source provenance tracking ensure verifiability in scientific literature synthesis?
expected_document_titles: Hallucination Mitigation in Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
GraphRAG: Unlocking LLM Discovery on Complex Information Networks
labeled_claims: Preserving page numbers and exact character offsets allows researchers to verify claims directly against primary source text.
Traceable citations prevent hallucinated attribution by binding every claim to a specific passage identifier.
